NONE: › If someone or something experiences ups and downs, a mixture of good and bad things happens to him, her, or it.
盛衰；沉浮

example: Like most married couples we've had our ups and downs, but life's like that.
和大多數已婚夫婦一樣，我們也經歷過沉浮波折，但生活就是如此。

NONE: › Upscale goods and products are of very high quality and intended to be bought by people who are quite rich.
（商品、產品）高檔的，高級的

example: an upscale brand name
高檔品牌
The old hotel has gone upscale in recent years.
這座老旅館近年來變高檔了。

NONE: › specialized business to try to persuade a customer who is already buying something to buy more, or to buy something more expensive
向上推銷（試圖說服顧客購買額外或者更昂貴的產品）

example: They are trained to upsell customers to a larger drink.
他們受到訓練如何勸說顧客購買更大量的飲料。

NONE: › specialized business the act of trying to persuade a customer who is already buying something to buy more, or to buy something more expensive
向上推銷（試圖說服顧客購買額外或者更昂貴的產品）

example: The salesmen always look for opportunities for upselling.
推銷員總是在找向上推銷的機會。

T: B2 to make someone worried, unhappy, or angry
使心煩意亂；使難過；使生氣
› to change the usual or expected state or order of something, especially in a way that stops it from happening or working

C: › [ C ] an occasion when someone beats the team or player that was expected to win

T: › to push or knock something out of its usual position, usually by accident, especially causing it to fall
› to make someone feel slightly sick

after verb: A2 [ after verb ] worried, unhappy, or angry
使心煩意亂；使難過；使生氣

NONE: B2 informal If you have an upset stomach you feel slightly ill, especially because of something you have eaten or drunk.
形容肚子不舒服（尤其因為吃喝的東西引起的不適）

C: › [ C ] informal a slight illness of the stomach

example: It still upsets him when he thinks about the accident.
一想起那次事故他仍很惱火。
Don't upset yourself by thinking about what might have been.
別再去想原本可能會怎樣了，何必自尋煩惱。
Any mechanical problems would upset our plans of driving across the desert.
哪怕是很小的機械故障都有可能攪亂我們駕車穿越沙漠的計劃。
Our dog upset the picnic table, spilling food everywhere.
狗撞翻了野餐桌，把我們的食物弄得到處都是。
He can't eat grapes - they upset him/his stomach.
他不能吃葡萄——他的胃受不了。
Don't get upset about the dress - there's only a little stain on it.
不要爲這條裙子難過了——上面只有一個小汙點而已。
[ + to infinitive ] She was very upset to hear that the party had been cancelled.
聽說聚會取消了，她很沮喪。
[ + that ] He was very upset that you didn't reply to his emails.
你沒給他回信，他很失望。
I have an upset stomach/tummy - serves me right for eating so much.
我肚子不舒服——我這是自作自受，誰讓自己吃得太多。
How much upset will the new monitoring procedures cause?
新的監控程序將會帶來多大的混亂?
It would be quite an upset if the favourite didn't win.
如果這個奪標大熱門沒有獲勝，那就真是爆冷門。
Melanie has a stomach/tummy upset so she won't be going to school today.
梅蘭妮肚子不舒服，所以今天不去上學了。

NONE: › to cause trouble, especially by spoiling someone's plans
製造麻煩；（尤指）打亂計劃
› making someone feel worried, unhappy, or angry
令人心煩意亂的，令人苦惱（或憤怒）的

example: Seeing her again would be an upsetting experience after so many years.
時隔這麽多年再見到她將是一次令人不快的經歷。

NONE: › someone who gets a job that is well paid and difficult because they no longer want to stay at home or do a job that is easy
（因不願待業在家或厭惡簡單的工作而）選擇難度大的高薪工作的人

example: Compare
downshift

NONE: › the advantage of a situation
優點；好處；有利的一面

example: It's annoying that we can't travel until Thursday, but the upside is that tickets are cheaper then.
煩人的是我們要等到週四才能出發去旅行，但好處是到時票價會便宜些。
Compare
downside

NONE: B2 having the part that is usually at the top turned to be at the bottom
上下顛倒（地），翻轉（地）

example: Turn the jar upside down and shake it.
把罐子倒過來，搖一搖。
The plane was flying upside down at high speed.
飛機正在倒飛，速度極快。

NONE: › the 20th letter of the Greek alphabet
（希臘語字母表的第20個字母）
› to learn new skills or to teach workers new skills
學習新技能；教授新技能

example: The program is aimed at people working in IT who want to upskill.
這一課程是針對在資訊科技行業工作、需要學習新技能的人的。
We are upskilling the team.
我們正在提高團隊的技能。

NONE: › the process of learning new skills or of teaching workers new skills
學習新技能；教授新技能
› to take people's attention away from someone and make them listen to or look at you instead
搶…的風頭
› towards or at the part of a theatre stage that is furthest from the people watching the performance
向舞臺後部（的）；在舞臺後部（的）

example: Most supporting bands tend to be youngsters, and rarely upstage the star.
大多數助興樂隊由年輕樂手組成，很少會搶歌星的風頭。
He looks upstage to where the body is lying.
他向舞臺後部屍體躺著的地方看去。
Opposite
downstage

NONE: A2 towards or on the highest floor or floors of a building
往樓上（地）；在樓上（地）

example: an upstairs landing/window
樓上的平臺／窗戶
He heard glass breaking and ran upstairs to see what had caused it.
聽到玻璃破碎的聲音，她跑上樓去看是怎麽回事。
Opposite
downstairs

NONE: › behaving in a good and moral way
正直的，正派的

example: She is regarded as an upstanding citizen in the local community.
當地社區認爲她是一位品行端正的好市民。

C: › disapproving a person, especially a young one, who has suddenly got power or an important position and takes advantage of this in an unpleasant way
（尤指年輕的）突然發跡的人，暴發戶；新貴

example: Larger drug companies are buying up many of the upstart companies.
大型藥企正在收購新興競爭公司。

NONE: › towards or of the northern parts of a state in the US, especially those that are far from cities where a lot of people live
（尤指美國邊遠地區）向（或在）州的北部（的）

example: The traffic going upstate was almost standing still.
前往州北部的交通幾乎停滯不動。

NONE: › (moving) on a river or stream towards its origin
在上游（地）；向上游（地）；逆流（地）
› relating to an earlier stage in a process or series of events
在（某過程或事件的）前階段

example: Salmon swim upstream against very strong currents to reach their breeding areas.
鮭魚會迎着湍急的水流游向它們在上游的産卵區。
The company's upstream business includes oil exploration and production.
這家公司的上游業務包括石油勘探和開採。

NONE: › a sudden and usually large increase in something
急劇上升，猛增

example: An upsurge of/in violence in the district has been linked to increased unemployment.
該地區暴力事件的猛增與失業率上升有關。

NONE: › an increase or improvement
上漲，上升；改善

example: Many analysts are predicting an upswing in the economy.
許多分析家預測經濟狀況將會好轉。
